newsitem.title: UK: Regulators barely keep up with industry - UK's SFA.
newsitem.headline: Regulators barely keep up with industry - UK's SFA.

text.p: Financial regulators are barely keeping up with the welter of changes occurring in the industry, and the solution may lie in looser rather than tighter regulations, a British watchdog said on Tuesday.

"We regulators are hard put to keep pace with the breaking down of old business boundaries -- between banking, securities, fund management and insurance," said Richard Farrant, chief executive of the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA).

Farrant, speaking at a conference here, said regulators are finding it hard to keep pace with the pressure on firms to cut corners, with innovative risk management techniques, and with the tendency to focus on detailed sets of rules rather than the aim of those rules.
He said the temptation was to seek to turn the regulatory screw more tightly.
"The better way may well be to loosen somewhat, if by doing so we can make the regulators, regulated firms and their management more directly accountable for their actions."

While regulators were responding to the changes, it was less certain whether the response would prove to be adequate to keep up with the sheer volume of upheaval in the industry. He added that change was set to accelerate in the next five to 10 years.
